newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks buoyed at close on year-end buying.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks buoyed at close on year-end buying.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed higher Friday, bolstered by light year-end buying.
"Today is when issuing companies close their books for the year, dealers rush to raise prices and some clients take advantage of the fact to buy low in advance," a dealer said.
"If it had been otherwise, the market would have been dead. Volume was thin, and most of that was in cross trades and same-day buy-sell trades," he added.
The blue chip IPC index closed up 16.31 points, or 0.49 percent, at 3,327.20. Volume was 52.2 million shares traded.
Analysts said Mexican stocks benefitted from gains on Wall Street and technical factors.
"The market is still very quiet. Today's gains were speculative and partly driven by the Dow Jones," said Hector Jimenez, an analyst with the Inverlat financial group.
"Furthermore, the IPC validated a breakthrough at 3,300 points. The next objective, which me may reach next week, is at 3,350 points, in order to try to close the year at 3,400." Jimenez said.
On the broad market, 109 stocks were traded, of which gainers outnumbered sliders by 62 to 24.

Tourist firm Situr headed the gainers, followed by its parent company, Sidek, in third place. The stocks ended up four centavos (1 cent) and seven centavos (1 cent), respectively, to 42 centavos (5 cents) and 97 centavos (12 cents).
"Situr and Sidek gained on buying by the companies them selves to improve their year-end prices. The trades were not very big," a dealer said.

Cement makers Ttolmex headed the sliders, followed by computer company Acerla, which ended off three pesos (38 cents) and 1.90 pesos (24 cents), respectively, at 30.00 ($3.82) and 29.60 pesos ($3.77).
"These were not very relevant changes," a dealer said.
